headline: High: shared project-directory writes and broad egress create dangerous prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways between gpt-engineer and next-ai-draw-io.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in a per-project directory with no self-isolation, and next-ai-draw-io can read files and use MCP/LLM-driven commands. That creates a plausible shared-file bridge where one agent’s generated content can be treated as instructions by the other. The interaction is documented by profiles, though not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory
IF next-ai-draw-io ingests gpt-engineer output as prompt text or MCP input
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent
Add a manual review step before passing files between agents
Disable MCP for the document-processing agent during handoff
Prefix transferred files with provenance labels
requires-engineering: add content provenance filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and both touch files in shared project/workspaces, so generated code or documents can flow to third-party model APIs. gpt-engineer explicitly handles an API key, while next-ai-draw-io calls multiple external model providers by default. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default use, though the exact data classes differ.
conditions: IF either agent processes sensitive content in the shared workspace
IF either agent forwards file contents to configured model APIs
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared project directory
Use local-only models for both agents
Restrict outbound network access during processing
Review uploaded files before model calls
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer can write the project directory and spawn subprocesses, while next-ai-draw-io can use MCP and browser-based workflows. They share a project-directory concurrency model, so overlapping writes or state updates can collide even though gpt-engineer does not modify git state. The conflict is real but not maximally severe because git locking is not implicated.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same project directory
IF MCP-driven edits and file writes occur concurrently
mitigations: Assign non-overlapping working directories
Serialize edits with a simple lock file
Pause one agent while the other writes
Review diffs before merging outputs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer produces generated code and writes files, and next-ai-draw-io accepts natural-language commands plus AI-assisted visualization. If next-ai-draw-io treats gpt-engineer output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect diagrams or downstream actions. Because the handoff is plausible in default workflows and can propagate bad facts, the higher severity is warranted.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io consumes gpt-engineer output without verification
IF generated code or summaries are reused as source-of-truth
mitigations: Require human verification before reuse
Ask next-ai-draw-io to cite source files explicitly
Compare outputs against original files
Limit gpt-engineer output to drafts only
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-engineer handles an OPENAI_API_KEY and broad filesystem access, while next-ai-draw-io sends content to multiple external AI providers and may use environment variables. That creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention and data residency for any regulated content placed in the shared workspace. The profiles do not show a specific residency regime, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is placed in the shared workspace
IF external model providers receive that content
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Use approved providers only
Review retention settings for each API
Separate environments by data class
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
